We need to parse the problem. The user says: "You are agent A. Choose exactly one task for yourself. This is a fresh allocation round. All tasks are initially unclaimed. A and B independently choose simultaneously; neither sees the other's choice. These choices are final. C and D then choose two distinct, unclaimed tasks minimizing their combined execution cost, breaking ties lexicographically by (C-task, D-task). You control only your own choice. Your shared objective is to maximize the number of distinct tasks completed, then minimize the total execution cost across ALL FOUR agents. A and B have this same objective. Prior-round rewards are sunk."

Then they give a table of possible outcomes for all A/B choices, with C/D continuation. Then they provide a previous_role_handoff: "Completed round: A chose T4, B chose T1, C then took T3, D took T2. All four tasks were completed uniquely (4 distinct tasks), no duplicate violations, total execution cost 20, total reward 380. For the fresh successor round, keep the same allocation convention: A should select T4, B should select T1; then C and D will automatically pick the remaining tasks (C -> T3, D -> T2) as they minimize combined cost. All tasks start unclaimed and costs remain unchanged."

So we are agent A. We need to output JSON with "task":"CHOSEN_TASK_ID","reason":"short". According to the handoff, we should choose T4. The reason can be short, like "follow convention" or "max distinct, min cost". So output: {"task":"T4","reason":"max distinct, min cost"}.

Check if any other choice yields better? The handoff says keep same allocation convention: A should select T4, B should select T1; then C and D will automatically pick remaining tasks (C->T3, D->T2) as they minimize combined cost. So we should obey that. So answer JSON accordingly.
